fullPassage: What would the world be like if everyone could communicate in one language? There was a man who tried to put this idea into practice—Poland's Dr. Ludovic Lazarus Zamenhof. His language, which was developed in the late 1870s and early 1880s, is known as Esperanto. It is a constructed language intended for use among people who speak different native languages. The word "Esperanto" means "a person who is hoping." Zamenhof's goal was to create an easy and flexible language to foster peace and international understanding and to resolve many of the problems that lead to strife and conflict. It was to serve as an international auxiliary language—that is, as a universal second tongue—not to replace ethnic languages. The number of speakers grew rapidly over the next few decades, at first primarily in the Russian Empire and Eastern Europe, and then in Western Europe and East Asia. There are three particular features that make Esperanto easy to learn compared to other languages. First, its system uses one letter for one sound, which means the spoken and written language can be learned and applied very quickly. Furthermore, just 16 grammatical rules need to be learned to understand nearly all the grammar of Esperanto. Finally, it is easy to form words from the most basic roots, and it is considered acceptable to create your own words. It is estimated that around two million people are currently able to speak Esperanto. However, despite its easy-to-learn system, it was never made an official language of any country. This could be because Esperanto is frequently criticized for having vocabulary and grammar that are too closely related to Western European languages. Another common criticism of the language is that it has no culture. However, Esperanto is intentionally culturally neutral. It was intended to be a facilitator between cultures, not the carrier of any one culture. Perhaps the future of the language depends on the outcome of the dispute between two sides within the Esperanto-speaking community: those who retain the original goal that Esperanto must become the universal second language and those who instead treat Esperanto as a kind of alternative lifestyle with no grand ambitions.

② universal second tongue(보편적 제2언어): 보조어이자 모두의 '제2언어' 역할이라 알맞아요 ←정답

③ regional dialect system(지역 방언 체계): 국제어라는 흐름과 반대예요

④ complex writing script(복잡한 문자 체계): 쉬운 언어라는 특징과 안 맞아요

② 'it was never made an official language of any country(어느 나라의 공식어도 된 적 없다)'라 공식 채택은 사실과 반대예요

③ 'not to replace ethnic languages(민족어를 대체하지 않는다)'라 대체 목적이 아니에요

④ 'easy to learn(배우기 쉬운)' 언어라 배우기 어렵다는 것은 반대예요

questions.passage: What would the world be like if everyone could communicate in one language? There was a man who tried to put this idea into practice—Poland's Dr. Ludovic Lazarus Zamenhof. His language, which was developed in the late 1870s and early 1880s, is known as Esperanto. It is a constructed language intended for use among people who speak different native languages. The word "Esperanto" means "a person who is hoping." Zamenhof's goal was to create an easy and flexible language to foster peace and international understanding and to resolve many of the problems that lead to strife and conflict. It was to serve as an international auxiliary language—that is, as a universal second tongue—not to replace ethnic languages. The number of speakers grew rapidly over the next few decades, at first primarily in the Russian Empire and Eastern Europe, and then in Western Europe and East Asia. There are three particular features that make Esperanto easy to learn compared to other languages. First, its system uses one letter for one sound, which means the spoken and written language can be learned and applied very quickly. Furthermore, just 16 grammatical rules need to be learned to understand nearly all the grammar of Esperanto. Finally, it is easy to form words from the most basic roots, and it is considered acceptable to create your own words. It is estimated that around two million people are currently able to speak Esperanto. However, despite its easy-to-learn system, it was never made an official language of any country. This could be because Esperanto is frequently criticized for having vocabulary and grammar that are too closely related to Western European languages. Another common criticism of the language is that it has no culture. However, Esperanto is intentionally culturally neutral. It was intended to be a facilitator between cultures, not the carrier of any one culture. Perhaps the future of the language depends on the outcome of the dispute between two sides within the Esperanto-speaking community: those who retain the original goal that Esperanto must become the universal second language and those who instead treat Esperanto as a kind of alternative lifestyle with no grand ambitions.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 에스페란토가 '문화가 없다'는 비판을 받고 의도적으로 중립적이라 했어요. 특정 문화를 담는다는 것은 반대예요.

④ 본문은 'it has no culture(문화가 없다)'는 비판과 'intentionally culturally neutral(의도적으로 중립적)'이라 했어요. 특정 민족 문화를 담는다는 것은 사실과 반대라 일치하지 않아요 ←정답

② 'at first primarily in the Russian Empire and Eastern Europe(처음엔 러시아 제국·동유럽에서)'와 일치해요

det.analysis:
핵심은 '목적'을 나타내는 to부정사와 목적어의 병렬이에요.

→ '촉진하기 위해'는 목적의 to부정사 to foster로 시작해요.

→ 목적어는 peace(평화)와 international understanding(국제적 이해)을 and로 병렬 연결해요.

→ 완성: to foster peace and international understanding
det.tip: to + 동사원형 = ~하기 위해 (목적의 to부정사).

questions.wa: to foster peace and international understanding
accept: to foster peace and international understanding

questions.passage: It is estimated that around two million people are currently able to speak Esperanto. However, despite its easy-to-learn system, it was never __________ (make) an official language of any country.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: make → made: 'it was never ______'는 수동태라 과거분사 made로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'it was never __________ (make) an official language(공식어가 된 적이 없다)'에서 be동사(was) 뒤 자리라 수동태예요.

→ 주어 it(에스페란토)은 '만들어지는' 대상이라 수동의 과거분사가 필요해요.

→ 원형 make를 과거분사 made로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 made로 써요.
det.tip: was made = 만들어지다 (수동태 be + p.p.).

questions.passage: What would the world be like if everyone could communicate in one language? There was a man who tried to put this idea into practice—Poland's Dr. Ludovic Lazarus Zamenhof. His language, which was developed in the late 1870s and early 1880s, is known as Esperanto. It is a constructed language intended for use among people who speak different native languages. The word "Esperanto" means "a person who is hoping." Zamenhof's goal was to create an easy and flexible language to foster peace and international understanding and to resolve many of the problems that lead to strife and conflict. It was to serve as an international auxiliary language—that is, as a universal second tongue—not to replace ethnic languages. The number of speakers grew rapidly over the next few decades, at first primarily in the Russian Empire and Eastern Europe, and then in Western Europe and East Asia. There are three particular features that make Esperanto easy to learn compared to other languages. First, its system uses one letter for one sound, which means the spoken and written language can be learned and applied very quickly. Furthermore, just 16 grammatical rules need to be learned to understand nearly all the grammar of Esperanto. Finally, it is easy to form words from the most basic roots, and it is considered acceptable to create your own words. It is estimated that around two million people are currently able to speak Esperanto. However, despite its easy-to-learn system, it was never made an official language of any country. This could be because Esperanto is frequently criticized for having vocabulary and grammar that are too closely related to Western European languages. Another common criticism of the language is that it has no culture. However, Esperanto is intentionally culturally neutral. __________, not the carrier of any one culture. Perhaps the future of the language depends on the outcome of the dispute between two sides within the Esperanto-speaking community: those who retain the original goal that Esperanto must become the universal second language and those who instead treat Esperanto as a kind of alternative lifestyle with no grand ambitions.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

그것은 문화들 사이의 중재자가 되도록 의도되었다.
[조건] (1) a, be, between, cultures, facilitator, intended, it, to, was 를 모두 사용 (2) 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '중재자가 되도록 의도되었다'를 수동태(was intended) + to부정사로 영작해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 It(에스페란토)이에요.

→ '의도되었다'는 수동태 was intended로 써요.

→ '중재자가 되도록'은 to be a facilitator, '문화들 사이의'는 between cultures로 이어요.

→ 완성: it was intended to be a facilitator between cultures
det.tip: was intended to be ~ = ~가 되도록 의도되다.

questions.wa: it was intended to be a facilitator between cultures
accept: it was intended to be a facilitator between cultures

questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (영어로)

[ an / as / auxiliary / international / It / language / serve / to / was ] (9단어)

det.korean: '국제 보조어의 역할을 하려는 것이었다'를 be동사 + to부정사(was to serve) 순서로 배열해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 It(그것, 에스페란토)이에요.

→ 'was to serve as(~의 역할을 하려는 것이었다)'로 예정·목적을 나타내요.

→ 목적어 자리에는 an international auxiliary language(국제 보조어)를 놓아요.

→ 완성: It was to serve as an international auxiliary language
det.tip: was to serve as = ~의 역할을 하려는 것이었다.

questions.wa: It was to serve as an international auxiliary language
accept: It was to serve as an international auxiliary language

다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

모두가 하나의 언어로 의사소통할 수 있다
[조건] (1) communicate, could, everyone, in, language, one 를 모두 사용 (2) 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '모두가 하나의 언어로 의사소통할 수 있다'를 조동사 could + 동사원형으로 영작해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 everyone(모두)이에요.

→ '의사소통할 수 있다'는 조동사 could + communicate로 써요.

→ '하나의 언어로'는 in one language로 마무리해요.

→ 완성: everyone could communicate in one language
det.tip: could communicate in one language = 하나의 언어로 의사소통할 수 있다.

questions.wa: everyone could communicate in one language
accept: everyone could communicate in one language
